title: Staged Traffic Proxy: client transactional SDK helpers for safe canary, A/B, and shadow rollouts
creator: Ana Patel
description:
Problem: Existing rollout primitives are server-side heavy and lack a compact client helper that (1) guarantees safe, idempotent control-plane operations for staged traffic changes, (2) provides an embeddable local 'staging proxy' for shadow traffic and preflight checks, and (3) integrates permission-aware ephemeral tokens for limited-scope rollout operations.

Goal: Build a Staged Traffic Proxy API plus small client SDK helpers that teams can embed in their control plane or CI to orchestrate canaries, A/B experiments, and shadow traffic experiments with deterministic idempotency and auto-rollback triggers. The proxy should be minimal, stateless for control operations (server reconciler owns final state), and provide strong auditing and permission scopes for production use.

This ticket covers the API surface, client helper primitives (idempotency tokens, local preview/stub proxy, sampling controls), migration guidance, and automated rollback hooks wired to runtime metrics. Implementation will live in rollout-service with an SDK package redwood-rollout-client for Node/Python initially.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New endpoints: POST /v1/rollout/proxy/initiate, POST /v1/rollout/proxy/adjust, POST /v1/rollout/proxy/commit, POST /v1/rollout/proxy/abort documented and implemented behind feature flag.
2) SDK helpers provide: idempotency-key header utility, ephemeral token exchange, local staging proxy binary (or dev-mode middleware) to replay shadow traffic, and an API to register metric-based rollback predicates.
3) End-to-end integration test that simulates a canary with 5% -> 50% ramp and triggers auto-rollback when latency p95 increases by >25% or error rate >2% absolute.
4) RBAC enforcement: tokens scoped to rollout:manage:project and rollout:preview; audit events emitted for every proxy action with request_id.
5) Documentation + migration guide and an example GitHub repo using the SDK to perform a canary rollout with auto-rollback.
6) Security review flagged and approved for ephemeral token flows.
rollout_flow:
1) Developer or CI obtains an ephemeral token scoped to project:rollout:preview or project:rollout:manage.
2) SDK helper creates a UUID idempotency key and calls /initiate with sampling config. The Staged Traffic Proxy returns a proxy_run_id and a signed routing token used by the runtime to accept staged traffic.
3) The SDK can run a local dev-mode staging proxy that mirrors or replays a percentage of live traffic (shadow) to the candidate model, collecting small-sample outputs and running canary checks locally before traffic allocation.
4) Control-plane executes weighted routing changes (5% -> 50%) via /adjust calls; each adjust is idempotent when using the same key and includes a monotonic seq number to protect against stale adjustments.
5) Monitoring hooks evaluate predicates; if any predicate fires and auto_rollback enabled, the proxy will emit an automatic abort with audit log and restore previous weights.
6) Finalize via /commit once the run meets promotion thresholds. The commit operation is idempotent and requires manage scope.

Edge cases: network partitions require the SDK to query /v1/rollout/proxy/status to reconcile. Proxy-run metadata retained for 7 days for auditing.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for idempotency de-duping and header validation. Integration tests that spin up a small staging proxy and a fake runtime to validate routing tokens. Chaos tests for delayed /abort to ensure rollback race conditions are safe. Load tests to ensure proxy does not become bottleneck (target 500 rps control-plane throughput). E2E test scenario: simulate 10k requests with 5% shadow sampling and assert that sampling overhead <3% p50 latency increase.

QA checklist: verify audit events in archive, assert RBAC denies tokens scoped to wrong project, verify expiration of ephemeral tokens, manual canary run with telemetry dashboard showing auto-rollback trigger firing.
migration_notes: For existing customers using declarative rollout manifests, provide a compatibility shim: the SDK will translate manifest changes into a sequence of idempotent proxy calls. Document recommended steps to rotate jobs that currently call admin endpoints directly to use ephemeral token exchange. Announce deprecation window (6 months) for legacy /v1/rollouts/admin endpoints used without idempotency keys.
